experiments.title: Does the cross-encoder reranker earn its cost?
experiments.subtitle: Week 4 — rerank ablation
experiments.narrative: Every metric improved when the cross-encoder reranker was layered on top of the BM25 + dense fused retrieval. Faithfulness went from 0.85 to 0.94 — the model hallucinates less when the prompt context is better-ranked. The reranker stayed in the pipeline.

experiments.title: Does the LangGraph agent beat the linear pipeline?
experiments.subtitle: Week 5 — first attempt, with DuckDuckGo web fallback enabled
experiments.narrative: The agent regressed on every metric. Per-question diagnosis showed two failure modes: the small local critic over-flagged sufficient context as 'insufficient' and over-triggered the loop, and when the loop exhausted, the DuckDuckGo web fallback fed off-domain snippets to the generator — faithfulness collapsed (-0.16) and the wrong context tanked recall (-0.14). The agent was not deploy-ready as-is.

experiments.title: Does disabling the web fallback close the regression?
experiments.subtitle: Week 5 — agent re-run, web fallback off, otherwise unchanged
experiments.narrative: Disabling the web fallback erased the regression on the two output-quality metrics. Faithfulness recovered by +0.14 (0.81 → 0.95, matching linear); answer relevancy followed suit. A small residual gap remains on the retrieval-side metrics (context precision and recall), attributable to the critic occasionally looping with a reformulated query that lands on slightly different chunks. The agent is now ship-ready on local Ollama, with further gains expected when the deployed pipeline uses Groq's 70B model as the critic.
